results.label: this tree ships the M12 rule-break tally (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the review ships a rule-break card and renders it as its own section
the totals line separates what happened: breaks, prevented attempts, accepted overrides, observed conditions and excluded legal records
every rule the audit named gets its own line, with its own prevented/accepted split rather than one blended number
the days are listed newest-first with their own split and the rules that fired on them
an undecodable snapshot is SHOWN as unreadable, not swallowed, and is never attributed to a rule
a break with no rule named in its snapshot is shown as counted-but-unnamed rather than attributed
a bounded read says so on screen instead of hiding rows behind a total
the framing the payload carries is rendered: it is not broker truth, not mental state, not a market edge, and it does not join a break to an outcome
the card makes NO percentage, causal or profitability claim of its own
a rule name from the audit is rendered as TEXT, not as markup (a hostile name cannot become an element)
an unreadable audit is rendered as UNKNOWN on screen: a warning, no zero total and no clean-week wording
an empty but readable audit reads as a recorded zero with its own sentence — and never as the unavailable shape
a payload with missing arrays (an older or partial shape) still renders instead of throwing
the reload button is present and refuses to act when the workspace moved under it: a stale review never reloads another account’s tally
the card binds itself to the trader’s own workspace/account/token, the guard the mismatch check above relies on
the review actually MOUNTS the card: the analytics view renders it and the page loads the script
the view is loaded after the helpers it uses and before the app boots, like every other aggregate card

scope: M12 real DOM: the rule-break card the review reads: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
